title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v119
author: Ethan Cole
release_notes:
- Add profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v119 for Benchmark Lab.
- New representative workload runners and updated perf suites.
- Instrumentation for adaptive batching signals and telemetry.
description:
Motivation: We need a repeatable baseline for profiling performance regressions across representative workloads and to surface reporting metrics in the Benchmark Lab dashboards. This PR adds profiling baselines (v119), representative workload runners for medium/large sequence families, and a reporting pipeline that aggregates per-run telemetry for automatic regression detection.

Changes in this PR: checklist:
- [x] Add profiling baseline definitions (cpu/gpu) and baseline metadata
- [x] Implement representative workload runners for conversation, summarization, and code-completion families
- [x] Add reporting pipeline job definitions and jobs to publish results to telemetry/backfill storage
- [x] Wire adaptive batching signals into the profiler outputs so the reporting pipeline can correlate batch size distribution with latency/regressions
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for the new runners and pipeline connectors
- [x] Update benchmark-lab README and dashboard config references

Testing and validation: I ran the full perf suite on a staging cluster (r2-large GPUs) and verified the profiling baselines match expected thresholds. End-to-end reporting pipeline ran in staging and produced aggregated CSV + protobuf outputs consumed by the benchmarking dashboard. CI: build/test/lint all passed; integration job flaked once and was re-run (see CI summary).

Rollout plan: deploy to benchmark-lab staging for one week, monitor regression alerts, then flip to production reporting with a canary (10% of runs) for two days before full rollout.

Notes: The baseline metadata files are versioned under benchmarks/baselines/v119. Representative runners are intentionally conservative (no aggressive batching) to keep baseline variance low. Future follow-ups: add cold-start profiling runners and a small k8s operator to schedule periodic runs (ENG-2202).
